_doc: Ground vehicles you build: a motorcycle, a car and a truck, in that order. They are NOT a faster horse — each one gives something up. The bike is the quickest thing on the planet and carries almost nothing; the car seats the people who travel with you and hates rough ground; the truck is the slowest of the three and is the only way to move a ship's hull across a valley. The horse row is here as the yardstick, not as something you build: it needs no fuel and climbs ground nothing on wheels will look at, so it is never strictly worse than any of them. Every material id below comes from data/resources.json and every station from data/refining.json's machines — there is ONE material chain in this game and it is that one. Read by js/vehicles.js.
_fuelDoc: Everything with an engine burns CHARCOAL in a gas producer — a campfire recipe (data/refining.json `burn_charcoal`), which is the point: a motorcycle must not be gated behind the fuel synthesiser, because that structure is the last one in the game. Lift Fuel is for ships and nothing else.

fuel.name: Charcoal
fuel._doc: `perKm` on each vehicle is units of charcoal per kilometre driven. A full tank is `tank` units; at zero the engine stops and you walk, which is the whole reason the horse never stops being useful.

_yardstickDoc: A mounted horse is moveSpeed (5.4) x mountSpeed (2.1) = 11.34 m/s, the same figure js/gear.js repeats as HORSE_PACE. Every vehicle below is measured against this row, and tests/ground-vehicles.test.js fails if the two drift apart.

horse.name: Trail Horse
horse.lore: Patient, unremarkable, and it does not care that the fuel bench is thirty kilometres away.

_ladderDoc: `speed` is metres a second on level open ground. `road` multiplies it on a made road, `offroad` on broken ground, and above `maxSlope` (rise over run) the wheels simply will not take it — that is the stat the horse wins and it is why a bike is useless in the hills. `carry` is extra units of load, `seats` is how many people ride along, `ford` is how deep the water may be before it drowns.

motorcycle.name: Trail Scrambler
motorcycle.lore: One seat, two wheels and an engine bolted where the sense used to be. Nothing on this planet is quicker across a flat.
motorcycle.gives: The fastest thing you will ever sit on, and the least charcoal to feed.
motorcycle.costs: It carries a satchel, it drowns in a stream, and the first real hill stops it dead.

car.name: Ridge Runabout
car.lore: A box on four wheels with glass in it. The only vehicle where the weather stays outside and everyone you travel with comes along.
car.gives: Four seats, a roof over the night, and a road speed nothing else touches.
car.costs: Off the road it wallows, it is thirsty, and it will not climb what the bike will not climb.

truck.name: Longbed Hauler
truck.lore: Six wheels, a flat bed and low gearing. It is the slowest thing you will build and the only one that can put a hull plate on the pad in one trip.
truck.gives: A bed that swallows a camp, water up to the axles, broken ground it barely notices, and it is the only vehicle that can haul a ship subsystem.
truck.costs: Slower than the other two, drinks more than both together, and it corners like a barge.

_repairDoc: Wear is gentle on purpose — this is not a survival sim. A vehicle at 0 condition still drives, it just gives up a third of its speed and eats fuel until you spend an evening on it.
_surfaceDoc: What js/vehicles.js multiplies `speed` by. Whoever wires the controller passes one of these names; anything unknown counts as open ground.
